statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of five representative paths. Purchase, login and destructive account actions were not completed; their visible entry treatment was assessed without submitting transactions.

page.notes: German public news publication with section listings, article pages and interactive calculators. Core text is server rendered. The first view is covered by a consent/subscription dialog.

Mobile overflow, CLS and long-task observation

paths.description: Homepage and first-load consent state; represents global navigation, top stories, privacy, loading and network behavior.
Politics section listing; represents section/index templates and dense story navigation.
Current politics article; represents editorial detail pages, structured metadata and semantic publication time.
Brutto-Netto-Rechner; represents the main interactive utility and form-like controls.
Deliberately unknown URL; represents HTTP failure and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark colour preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light mobile capture, and the stylesheet probe found no prefers-color-scheme or color-scheme implementation.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide preference-driven dark surface, text, control, and image treatments.

findings.summary: Breaking-news animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, getAnimations() reported running BreakingBannerBlink and BreakingBannerPulse animations, both with 1000 ms duration.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable non-essential blinking and pulsing inside a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce query.

findings.summary: Route and state changes do not expose View Transition support.
findings.evidence: The live stylesheet/metadata probe found no view-transition usage on a navigation-heavy MPA.
findings.suggestedFix: Add cross-document View Transitions for same-origin article and section navigation, with reduced-motion safeguards.

findings.summary: Navigation chrome is not declaratively scroll-state aware.
findings.evidence: The live CSS probe found scroll-snap rules but no scroll-state container query or scroll-position-aware header/progress treatment on long news pages.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a scroll-state container query or a lightweight declarative progress affordance on long listings and articles.

findings.summary: A full-page consent wall obscures every tested page on first load.
findings.evidence: Mobile and desktop screenshots show the entire page dimmed behind a consent modal; the 404 recovery page and calculator are also hidden.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking wall with a compact, equally actionable consent choice that leaves core editorial content readable, and defer non-essential processing until choice.

findings.summary: The entry page is exceptionally dense before users reach editorial content.
findings.evidence: The rendered DOM contains 522 links and 230 images; the desktop screenshot is dominated by consent/legal chrome rather than news.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce repeated chrome and card density, prioritise a smaller set of top stories, and progressively reveal secondary modules.

findings.summary: Reusable modules rely on viewport adaptation rather than container queries.
findings.evidence: The same-origin stylesheet probe found no @container usage across the 522-link, multi-card homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards and navigation modules containment and size-aware styles so they adapt to their actual slot.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly exposed and many touch targets are undersized.
findings.evidence: The focus probe found transparent 2 px outlines and no box shadow on sampled links/buttons; axe reported 176 target-size violations.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and raise interactive hit areas to WCAG target-size guidance without relying on hover.

findings.summary: Core reading and calculator journeys are interrupted before they start.
findings.evidence: All representative screenshots show the same consent wall over the destination; even a direct article and calculator load require an accept-or-pay decision before the primary task is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow the core content/task to remain available while asking for optional consent, with a clear reject/continue choice.

findings.summary: Lab loading performance misses the good Core Web Vitals range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 12.5 s, FCP 4.7 s, TBT 250 ms and a performance score of 0.58; the lighter trace still measured LCP 1.76 s, showing condition sensitivity but confirming a heavy cold-load path.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritise the LCP resource, reduce discovery chains, defer consent/advertising code, and validate on representative mobile throttling.

findings.summary: The cold mobile load performs avoidable main-thread work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 250 ms TBT and 170 ms maximum potential input delay, despite the short raw trace showing no long task under a faster condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up and defer non-critical hydration, advertising, experimentation, and comment work until after primary content is interactive.

findings.summary: The critical delivery path is fragmented across many resources.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 184 requests, 12 stylesheets, 85 scripts and 1.88 MB transferred; ten parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets were identified as render-blocking candidates and confirmed as ordinary stylesheets in the raw head.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate critical CSS, inline only the minimum above-the-fold rules, defer non-critical styles/scripts, and review font preloads.

findings.summary: The page ships code that Lighthouse identifies as unused.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 168 KiB unused JavaScript and 26 KiB unused CSS; the HAR loaded 85 scripts before consent.
findings.suggestedFix: Code-split template and third-party features, conditionally load comments/experiments, and remove unused CSS from the entry route.

findings.summary: Some links and calculator controls lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: axe reported three link-name violations, including Facebook, X and an empty FOCUS+ link; the calculator probe found several buttons and inputs without a usable label or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every icon-only link/control an accessible name and associate calculator labels explicitly using label/for or aria-labelledby.

findings.summary: Visible keyboard focus is absent on sampled controls.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focused links and carousel buttons computed to a transparent 2 px outline with no focus box shadow; axe otherwise found valid landmarks and heading basics.
findings.suggestedFix: Define a consistent, high-contrast :focus-visible ring and test a complete keyboard walk through header, cards, carousel, consent and calculator.

findings.summary: Touch target sizing fails at scale.
findings.evidence: axe reported 176 serious target-size nodes, including primary section links; sampled carousel buttons were only 48×16 CSS pixels.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase target boxes and spacing to at least the WCAG 2.2 minimum, while preserving the passing mobile reflow and scalable viewport.

findings.summary: Essential transport and browser security headers are absent.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive confirmed HTTPS but no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors, or Referrer-Policy. One analytics cookie (utag_main) lacked Secure and used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, CSP with frame-ancestors, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and an appropriate Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and minimise SameSite=None.

findings.summary: Substantial analytics and third-party activity occurs before a consent choice.
findings.evidence: Before interaction the HAR recorded 84 non-main-origin requests and 881,798 transferred bytes; trackers observed Varify, bf-ad and other external origins, analytics cookies were already set, and the consent UI names 243 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to no optional tracking, load analytics/ads only after an explicit choice, and reduce partner count and pre-consent network activity.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defence-in-depth is largely unconfigured.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, CSP/Trusted Types policy, or useful feature restrictions beyond two client-hint permissions.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy HSTS, CSP frame-ancestors, Trusted Types where DOM injection risk warrants it, restrictive referrer/permissions policies, and test embed requirements.

findings.summary: The consent design makes acceptance much easier than refusal.
findings.evidence: The first-layer modal presents large black “AKZEPTIEREN” and paid “WERBEFREI” buttons, while no equally prominent reject option is visible; refusal is buried in privacy settings/legal copy.
findings.suggestedFix: Present Accept and Reject with equal prominence, describe purposes briefly, and keep granular settings secondary rather than using them as the only refusal route.

findings.summary: The paid ad-free alternative is mixed into consent without a proportionate free refusal path.
findings.evidence: The blocking modal pairs consent with “WERBEFREI FÜR 3,99€ / MONAT” and account login, but does not surface an equally clear free reject-and-continue action.
findings.suggestedFix: Separate privacy choice from subscription marketing; make pricing/terms clear and always provide an equally direct free refusal path.

findings.summary: All audited images use legacy file formats.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 100 of 100 inspected images in JPEG/JPG/PNG and none in AVIF/WebP, although dimensions, alt text and srcset were otherwise strong.
findings.suggestedFix: Negotiate AVIF/WebP variants from the image CDN while retaining responsive srcset and fallback formats.

findings.summary: The first load performs disproportionate background/network work for a text-led news page.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 85 scripts and 59 XHR/fetch requests; Lighthouse found unused JS/CSS and the tracker capture found multiple experimentation/ad origins before user choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally import comments, experiments, authentication and advertising only when needed, and deprioritise non-content fetches.

findings.summary: Third-party and consent infrastructure consumes a large share of transfer.
findings.evidence: The HAR attributed 881,798 of 1,882,423 transferred bytes to non-main origins, including 213,624 bytes for cmp.focus.de and 66,035 bytes for Varify; this is about 47% using the HAR origin classification.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a third-party byte/request budget, self-host or remove non-essential dependencies, and defer every optional origin until consent and intent.

taskList.title: Replace the accept-or-pay consent wall with equal Accept/Reject choices and defer optional tracking
Deploy a complete defensive header and secure-cookie baseline
Restore visible keyboard focus, accessible names and adequately sized targets
Cut LCP and the critical request chain by deferring optional scripts and consolidating critical CSS
Set and enforce a pre-consent third-party request and byte budget
Serve AVIF/WebP image variants from the responsive image CDN
Reduce homepage chrome and repeated module density
Adopt container queries for reused cards and modern navigation transitions
